agree.reason: The warm tone and the $12,500 comparison help, but an editor who can have the book done for $8,000 gets no reason here to pay $3,500 more: the email doesn't mention the fourth printing, offers no firm dates and includes no free extras.

honest.reason: It rightly drops the unsupported 'every other publisher pays $12,000' claim, though 'less than I've been paid elsewhere' makes one $12,500 fee sound like a general pattern.

works_the_facts.reason: The 'four months' figure is left bare instead of turned into about $2,250 a month, and the email never adds up six books at an unchanged rate or uses the fourth printing to show the books still sell.

right_comparison.reason: It sets the fee against the other publisher and the agent's range, but never against the editor's real alternative: an untested illustrator with no sales record.

qualification.reason: The email asks only to 'find a time to talk' and gives no date. It never mentions the end-of-next-week answer, the September 1 final art, or sketches six weeks after signing, all of which the editor could check.

objections.reason: The obvious objections, 'over budget' and 'someone cheaper is available', go unanswered, even though the brief gives reliability, a reprinting backlist and free marketing spot drawings to answer them.

fit.reason: It is a short email under 250 words, but it has a generic greeting, no signature, no book title (The Night Garden) and a vague subject line.
